modelEssay.title: Why Students Should Be Encouraged to Develop the Ability to Meet Challenges
modelEssay.content: In today's rapidly changing world, the ability to meet challenges is of paramount importance for students. Firstly, challenges serve as a catalyst for personal growth and development. Students who can overcome obstacles are more likely to build resilience and adaptability, which are crucial for success in both their academic and professional lives. Moreover, facing challenges head-on fosters creativity and problem-solving skills. These skills are not only valuable in the classroom but also indispensable in the real world, where complex issues require innovative solutions. In conclusion, equipping students with the ability to tackle challenges is essential for their holistic development and future success. It is imperative that educators and parents encourage and support students in developing this vital skill set.

structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：讨论挑战对个人成长和创造力培养的积极作用
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：总结学生面对挑战能力的重要性，并强调教育者和家长的支持作用

highlights: 使用了'paramount importance'等高级词汇
运用了'Firstly, Moreover'等连接词使文章结构清晰
逻辑清晰，过渡自然，有效连接了挑战与个人成长的关系

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话1。

transcript.text: Good morning, Safe House Insurance.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 早上好，Safe House 保险公司。

transcript.text: My name is Paul.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我叫保罗。

transcript.text: How can I help you today?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今天有什么可以帮您？

transcript.text: Morning.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 早上好。

transcript.text: I wouldn't say that is good from where I am standing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 从我这边的情况来看，这个早上可说不上好。

transcript.text: This is Miss Wilson, and this is the third time I've called this week.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我是威尔逊小姐，这已经是我这周打来的第三个电话了。

transcript.text: Since receiving your letter about our insurance claim, I'm getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 自从收到你们关于保险索赔的信函后，我对我的电话询问被完全无视感到有点受够了。

transcript.text: Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 威尔逊小姐，感谢您再次来电。

transcript.text: Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我能记录一些信息以协助我查看您的索赔吗？

transcript.text: It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South C Road in Cornwall, and the details are that our village was extensively flooded two months ago.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我是梅·威尔逊小姐，地址是康沃尔郡南C路15号。情况是两个月前我们村庄遭受了大面积洪灾。

transcript.text: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们小屋的整个一楼都被水淹没了。

transcript.text: And five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 从那以后，我们五个人一直住在一辆活动房车上。

transcript.text: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail, and it's not acceptable, Paul.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你们这些人却因为一个离奇的技术细节，仍然扣着我们有权获得的钱不给，这让人无法接受，保罗。

transcript.text: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 威尔逊小姐，根据您账户上的记录，您提到的那个离奇的技术细节指的是，事发前一个月您没有缴纳房屋保险费。

transcript.text: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you are suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那笔钱已经从我们账户划走了，而现在到了你们该赔付的时候，你们却突然说没有按时收到这笔钱。

transcript.text: I'm really sceptical about this claim.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我对此深表怀疑。

transcript.text: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 合同上确实说明，一年内任何一次未缴款都会影响保险合同的条款和条件，并可能影响索赔。

transcript.text: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 当然，我可以将您转接给我的经理，让他与您进一步讨论此事。

transcript.text: I've already spoken to him, and you can tell him I'm furious now and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我已经和他谈过了，你可以告诉他我现在非常愤怒，并且你们公司将面临诉讼。

transcript.text: You will be hearing from my lawyer.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你会收到我律师的函件。

transcript.text: Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 再见。

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话2。

transcript.text: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你对人工智能的未来有何看法？

transcript.text: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 就我个人而言，我对此相当乐观。

transcript.text: AI?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人工智能？

transcript.text: I'm not so optimistic, actually.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 实际上，我不那么乐观。

transcript.text: In fact, it's something we should be concerned about.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，这是我们应该担心的事情。

transcript.text: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，它将帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。

transcript.text: And when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而当我们更好地了解自己时，我们可以改善世界。

transcript.text: Well, one thing is for sure.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，有一件事是肯定的。

transcript.text: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 技术的发展速度超过了我们理解它的能力。

transcript.text: And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在未来，人工智能会让工作变得有点无意义。

transcript.text: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time, and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新型工作，这些工作需要的时间更少，并让我们专注于创造性任务。

transcript.text: I doubt that very much.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我非常怀疑这一点。

transcript.text: Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 可能最后剩下的工作将是编写人工智能软件。

transcript.text: And then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 然后最终，人工智能将自己编写自己的软件。

transcript.text: At that time, we are going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 到那时，我们将有很多没人愿意做的工作。

transcript.text: So we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys like us.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以我们需要人工智能让机器人照顾像我们这样的老人。

transcript.text: I don't know.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我不知道。

transcript.text: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 有一种风险是，人类文明可能被一种更高级的数字生命所取代。

transcript.text: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人工智能将能够完全模拟一个人，以所有可能的方式。

transcript.text: In fact, some people think we're in a simulation right now.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，有些人认为我们现在就在模拟中。

transcript.text: That's impossible.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那不可能。

transcript.text: Humans can't even make a mosquito.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人类甚至造不出一只蚊子。

transcript.text: Computers only have chips.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 计算机只有芯片。

transcript.text: People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人们有大脑，智慧就来源于此。

transcript.text: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 一旦完全发展，人工智能会厌倦尝试与人类沟通，因为相比之下，我们的思维要慢得多。

transcript.text: I'm not so sure.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我不太确定。

transcript.text: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 计算机就是计算机，计算机只是一个玩具。

transcript.text: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 计算机可以轻松地进行极其快速的通信。

transcript.text: So the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以计算机在与人类交谈时会变得不耐烦。

transcript.text: It'll be barely getting any information out.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它几乎得不到任何信息。

transcript.text: Well, I believe there's a benevolent future with AI.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，我相信人工智能有一个仁慈的未来。

transcript.text: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我也认为你看太多科幻电影了。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 文章一。

transcript.text: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
transcript.translation: 要实现财务安全，你储蓄的金额永远比你赚多少钱或投资多精明更重要。

transcript.text: If you're under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
transcript.translation: 如果你不到30岁，你的目标应该是每月储蓄税后收入的20%。

transcript.text: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
transcript.translation: 这与你的收入多少无关。

transcript.text: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
transcript.translation: 大约50%应预留用于食物和住房等基本开支。

transcript.text: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
transcript.translation: 剩下的30%用于休闲娱乐。

transcript.text: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
transcript.translation: 但对许多年轻人来说，将如此大比例的收入指定用于储蓄是困难的。

transcript.text: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
transcript.translation: 如果你觉得存钱很难，那就从削减所有不必要的开支开始。

transcript.text: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 % for savings and gradually increase that amount.
transcript.translation: 先分配一小笔1%或2%用于储蓄，并逐渐增加这个金额。

transcript.text: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
transcript.translation: 要始终牢记20%的目标，以防自己变得自满。

transcript.text: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
transcript.translation: 坚持这样一个严格的计划可能具有挑战性。

transcript.text: But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
transcript.translation: 但如果你采取正确的心态，你应该能让它为你所用。

transcript.text: So what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
transcript.translation: 那么，你应该用你存下来的钱做什么呢？

transcript.text: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
transcript.translation: 一部分必须保持易于取用，以备紧急需要现金。

transcript.text: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
transcript.translation: 最大比例应投资于退休计划，无论是通过你的雇主还是私下进行。

transcript.text: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
transcript.translation: 并且你可以保留一些钱用于高风险但可能带来丰厚回报的投资。

transcript.text: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
transcript.translation: 股息可以再投资，或用于购买你喜欢的东西。

transcript.text: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now and still be financially secure in the future.
transcript.translation: 遵循这个计划，你应该有望既能享受当下的生活，又能确保未来的财务安全。

transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: I work in advertising and I like to keep up with current trends, mainly because I'm aware that we live in an image-obsessed world.
transcript.translation: 我从事广告行业，喜欢跟上当前潮流，主要是因为我知道我们生活在一个痴迷于形象的世界。

transcript.text: However, when I first started my job, occasionally I'd catch a glimpse of myself in the lifts and find myself thinking that I looked a total mess.
transcript.translation: 然而，当我刚开始工作时，偶尔在电梯里瞥见自己，会觉得自己看起来一团糟。

transcript.text: Was I being held back by my choice of clothing?
transcript.translation: 是我的服装选择阻碍了我吗？

transcript.text: The short answer is yes, especially when clients are quick to judge you on your style rather than your work.
transcript.translation: 简短的回答是肯定的，尤其是当客户更倾向于根据你的风格而不是工作来评判你时。

transcript.text: But no one can be unique with their outfit every day.
transcript.translation: 但没有人能每天都穿着独特的服装。

transcript.text: I mean, that's why uniforms were invented.

transcript.text: So, here's what I did.

transcript.text: I created my own uniform.
transcript.translation: 我创造了自己的制服。

transcript.text: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
transcript.translation: 为此，我选择了一套合适的服装。

transcript.text: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
transcript.translation: 然后我买了多件相同风格但不同色调的衣服。

transcript.text: Now, I never worry about what I'm wearing in the morning, even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
transcript.translation: 现在，我从不担心早上穿什么，即使我确实有点厌倦只穿同样的经典款式。

transcript.text: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself, would looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
transcript.translation: 总的来说，当涉及到工作时，你必须问自己，看起来更聪明会提升我的工作能力吗？

transcript.text: For some, this question may not be an issue at all, especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face-to-face.
transcript.translation: 对某些人来说，这可能根本不是问题，尤其是如果你远程工作，很少与同事或客户面对面见面。

transcript.text: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
transcript.translation: 但如果你的工作涉及与其他人互动，答案通常是肯定的。

transcript.text: So, rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
transcript.translation: 所以，我认为与其对抗这个体系，我们不如做任何有助于实现工作目标的事情。

transcript.text: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let's face it, it's probably worth it.
transcript.translation: 如果这意味着在形象上保持稳妥，那么面对现实吧，这可能是值得的。

transcript.text: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
transcript.translation: 你知道吗，美国人拥有的空间大约是50年前的三倍？

transcript.text: Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
transcript.translation: 因此，你会认为我们有足够空间存放所有物品。

transcript.text: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
transcript.translation: 相反，个人储物业务现在是一个增长中的行业。

transcript.text: We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
transcript.translation: 我们有了三倍的空间，但我们已成为如此热情的消费者，以至于我们需要更多。

transcript.text: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half-century.
transcript.translation: 这一现象导致了显著的信用卡债务、巨大的环境足迹，或许并非巧合，我们的幸福水平在同一半个世纪里未能提升。

transcript.text: I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
transcript.translation: 我在此提出一个替代方案，即拥有更少可能实际上是一个更可取的决定。

transcript.text: Many of us have experienced at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
transcript.translation: 我们许多人在某个阶段都体验过拥有更少的快乐。

transcript.text: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economise, but also simplify your life.
transcript.translation: 我提议，更少的东西和更少的空间不仅能帮你节省开支，还能简化你的生活。

transcript.text: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
transcript.translation: 我最近开始了一个创新项目，以发现一些能提供我所需一切的创意解决方案。

transcript.text: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square metres instead of 60, I immediately saved $200 ,000.
transcript.translation: 通过购买一套40平方米而非60平方米的公寓，我立即节省了20万美元。

transcript.text: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills and also a smaller carbon footprint.
transcript.translation: 更小的空间导致更低的水电费账单，以及更小的碳足迹。

transcript.text: Because it's designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favourite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
transcript.translation: 因为它是围绕一个精选的物品收藏设计的，仅限于我最喜欢的东西，我真的很兴奋住在那里。

transcript.text: How can we live more basically?
transcript.translation: 我们如何能更基本地生活？

transcript.text: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
transcript.translation: 首先，我们必须无情地将不必要的物品从生活中剔除。

transcript.text: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy and ask ourselves, will it truly make me happier?
transcript.translation: 为了抑制消费，我们应该在购买前思考，并问自己，它真的会让我更快乐吗？

transcript.text: Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
transcript.translation: 显然，我们应该拥有一些好东西，但我们想要的是我们会长期喜爱的物品。

transcript.text: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
transcript.translation: 其次，我们需要空间效率。

transcript.text: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
transcript.translation: 我们想要的是设计用于大部分时间使用的电器，而不是偶尔使用的。

transcript.text: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
transcript.translation: 为什么拥有一个六灶头的炉子，而你很少使用甚至三个灶头？

transcript.text: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
transcript.translation: 最后，我们需要多功能空间和家居用品。

transcript.text: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
transcript.translation: 我将移动墙与变形家具结合起来，以充分利用有限空间。

transcript.text: Consider my coffee table.
transcript.translation: 考虑一下我的咖啡桌。

transcript.text: It increases in size to accommodate 10.
transcript.translation: 它可以扩大尺寸以容纳10人。

transcript.text: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
transcript.translation: 我的办公室被隐藏起来，易于隐藏。

transcript.text: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
transcript.translation: 我的床直接从墙里弹出来。

transcript.text: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilise the foldable guest beds I installed.
transcript.translation: 对于客人，我可以重新定位移动墙，并利用我安装的折叠客床。

transcript.text: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
transcript.translation: 我并不是说我们都应该住在小公寓里，但考虑一下精选生活的好处。

transcript.text: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves, could I do with a little live editing?

transcript.text: Would that give me more freedom and more time?
transcript.translation: 那会给我更多自由和时间吗？

transcript.text: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation, even if it hurts them to do so.
transcript.translation: 信不信由你，人们有时会为了保持良好、诚实的声誉而撒谎，即使这样做会伤害他们自己。

transcript.text: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
transcript.translation: 至少，这是一个科学家团队提出的观点，并有证据支持。

transcript.text: Picture this scenario.
transcript.translation: 想象一下这个场景。

transcript.text: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
transcript.translation: 你经常因工作开车，每月最多可报销400英里。

transcript.text: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month, but this month you drove 400 miles.
transcript.translation: 你公司的大多数人每月开车约300英里，但这个月你开了400英里。

transcript.text: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
transcript.translation: 你认为你会在费用报告中申报多少英里？

transcript.text: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today, with surprising results.
transcript.translation: 科学家在我们今天讨论的研究中提出了这个确切的问题，结果令人惊讶。

transcript.text: They found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
transcript.translation: 他们发现12%的受访者报告的行驶距离低于实际数字，平均答案为384英里。

transcript.text: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
transcript.translation: 换句话说，他们谎报了英里数，即使这会使他们损失应得的钱。

transcript.text: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high-expense claim.
transcript.translation: 研究人员认为这是为了显得诚实，假设是他人会对高额费用申报持怀疑态度。

transcript.text: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
transcript.translation: 但为什么人们会编造数字来损害自己的利益呢？

transcript.text: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
transcript.translation: 研究人员解释说，许多人非常关心自己的声誉以及他人如何评判他们。

transcript.text: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
transcript.translation: 如果他们足够关心，他们对显得诚实而不失去他人尊重的担忧可能超过他们实际诚实的欲望。

transcript.text: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
transcript.translation: 研究人员断言，研究结果表明，当人们获得非常有利的结果时，他们会预期他人的怀疑反应，宁愿撒谎显得诚实，也不愿说实话而被视为自私的骗子。

transcript.text: So why is this research important?
transcript.translation: 那么为什么这项研究重要呢？

transcript.text: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie, selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
transcript.translation: 嗯，专家们普遍同意有两种主要类型的谎言：自私的谎言和为了利益他人的谎言。

transcript.text: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others.
transcript.translation: 第一种，如你所料，是为了自私的利益，例如向保险公司提交欺诈性索赔；而第二种涉及为了帮助他人或不冒犯他人而撒谎。

transcript.text: For example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
transcript.translation: 例如，告诉一个你不喜欢其着装的朋友他们看起来很棒。

transcript.text: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying, lying to maintain a good reputation.
transcript.translation: 但研究人员提出了第三种类型的撒谎：为了维护良好声誉而撒谎。

transcript.text: Now, this hypothesis is new, and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie, but the findings seem intuitive to me.
transcript.translation: 现在，这个假设是新的，一些怀疑论者认为这并不是一个全新的谎言类别，但对我来说，这些发现似乎很直观。

transcript.text: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
transcript.translation: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一是增加我们在他人眼中的价值。

transcript.text: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
transcript.translation: 因此，人们为了显得诚实而撒谎的可能性很高。

transcript.text: Why do old people dislike new music?
transcript.translation: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

transcript.text: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like they just don't make good music like they used to.
transcript.translation: 随着年龄增长，我经常听到同龄人说类似的话，比如他们只是不再像过去那样制作好音乐了。

transcript.text: Why does this happen?
transcript.translation: 为什么会这样？

transcript.text: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
transcript.translation: 幸运的是，心理学可以为我们提供一些对这个谜题的见解。

transcript.text: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14, and by the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
transcript.translation: 音乐品味早在13或14岁就开始形成，到20岁出头时，这些品味就相当牢固地固定下来。

transcript.text: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
transcript.translation: 事实上，研究发现，到我们33岁时，大多数人已经停止听新音乐。

transcript.text: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group for the rest of your life.
transcript.translation: 同时，你在青少年早期流行的歌曲很可能在你一生中在同龄群体中保持相当流行。

transcript.text: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there's evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms, and melodies deteriorates with age.
transcript.translation: 这可能有生物学解释，因为有证据表明，大脑在区分不同和弦、节奏和旋律方面的能力随着年龄增长而衰退。

transcript.text: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all sound the same.
transcript.translation: 所以对老年人来说，较新的、不太熟悉的歌曲可能听起来都一样。

transcript.text: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
transcript.translation: 但老年人对新音乐的厌恶可能有一些更简单的原因。

transcript.text: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the mere exposure effect, which in essence means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
transcript.translation: 社会心理学中研究最多的定律之一叫做单纯曝光效应，本质上意味着我们接触某物越多，就越倾向于喜欢它。

transcript.text: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see, and the songs we listen to.
transcript.translation: 这种情况发生在我们认识的人、我们看到的广告和我们听的歌曲上。

transcript.text: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
transcript.translation: 当你在青少年早期时，你可能花相当多的时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

transcript.text: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
transcript.translation: 你最喜欢的歌曲和艺术家成为你日常生活中熟悉、令人安慰的部分。

transcript.text: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase.
transcript.translation: 对于许多30岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭责任增加。

transcript.text: So there's less time to spend discovering new music.
transcript.translation: 所以用于发现新音乐的时间就更少了。

transcript.text: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
transcript.translation: 相反，许多人只会听那个有更多空闲时间的时期的老旧、熟悉的最爱歌曲。

transcript.text: Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
transcript.translation: 当然，那些青少年岁月不一定无忧无虑。

transcript.text: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
transcript.translation: 它们以混乱著称，这就是为什么这么多电视节目和电影围绕高中动荡展开。

transcript.text: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
transcript.translation: 心理学研究表明，我们在青少年时期经历的情感似乎比后来更强烈。

transcript.text: And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
transcript.translation: 我们也知道，强烈的情感与更强的记忆和偏好相关联。

transcript.text: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
transcript.translation: 这两点都可能解释为什么我们在这个时期听的歌曲变得如此难忘和受人喜爱。

transcript.text: So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
transcript.translation: 所以，你的父母不喜欢你的音乐并没有什么错。

transcript.text: Rather, it's all part of the natural order of things.
transcript.translation: 相反，这都是事物自然秩序的一部分。

paragraphs.text: The idea of taxing things that are bad for society has a powerful allure. It offers the possibility of a double benefit— __26__ harmful activities, while also providing the government with revenue.
paragraphs.translation: 对有害社会的事物征税的想法具有强大的吸引力。它提供了双重好处的可能性——既阻止有害活动，又为政府提供收入。

paragraphs.text: Take sin taxes. Taxes on alcohol make it more expensive to get drunk, which reduces excessive drinking and __27__ driving. At the same time, they provide state and local governments with billions of dollars of revenue. Tobacco taxes, which generate more than twice as much, have proven __28__ in the decline of smoking, which has saved millions of lives.
paragraphs.translation: 以罪恶税为例。对酒精征税使得醉酒的成本更高，从而减少过度饮酒和酒后驾驶。同时，它们为州和地方政府提供了数十亿美元的收入。烟草税产生的收入是酒精税的两倍多，已被证明在吸烟率下降中发挥了重要作用，拯救了数百万人的生命。

paragraphs.text: Taxes can also be an important tool for environmental protection, and many economists say taxing carbon would be the best way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Economic theory says that unlike income or sales taxes, carbon taxes can actually increase economic efficiency; because companies that __29__ carbon dioxide into the sky don't pay the costs of the climate change they cause, carbon taxes would restore the proper __30__ to the market.
paragraphs.translation: 税收也可以是环境保护的重要工具，许多经济学家认为对碳征税是减少温室气体排放的最佳方式。经济理论指出，与所得税或销售税不同，碳税实际上可以提高经济效率；因为向大气中排放二氧化碳的公司没有承担它们造成的气候变化的成本，碳税会恢复市场的适当激励。

paragraphs.text: In reality, carbon taxes alone won't be enough to halt global warming, but they would be a useful part of any climate plan. What's more, the revenue from this tax, which would __31__ be hundreds of billions of dollars per year, could be handed out to citizens as a __32__ or used to fund green infrastructure projects.
paragraphs.translation: 实际上，仅靠碳税不足以阻止全球变暖，但它们将是任何气候计划的有用组成部分。更重要的是，这项税收的收入（可能每年数千亿美元）可以作为红利发放给公民，或用于资助绿色基础设施项目。

paragraphs.text: Similarly, a wealth tax has been put forward as a way to reduce inequality while raising revenue. The revenue from this tax, which some experts __33__ will be over $4 trillion per decade, would be designated for housing, child care, health care and other government benefits. If you believe, as many do, that wealth inequality is __34__ bad, then these taxes improve society while also __35__ government coffers (金库).
paragraphs.translation: 同样，财富税被提出作为一种既能减少不平等又能增加收入的方式。这项税收的收入（一些专家预测每十年将超过4万亿美元）将用于住房、儿童保育、医疗保健和其他政府福利。如果你像许多人一样认为财富不平等本质上是坏事，那么这些税收改善了社会，同时也充实了政府金库。

questionGroups.title: The Challenges for Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture

material.title: The Challenges for Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture

paragraphs.text: A group of corn farmers stands huddled around an agronomist (农学家) and his computer on the side of an irrigation machine in central South Africa. The agronomist has just flown over the field with a hybrid unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) that takes off and lands using propellers yet maintains distance and speed for scanning vast hectares of land through the use of its fixed wings.
paragraphs.translation: 一群玉米种植者聚集在南非中部一台灌溉机旁的农学家和他的电脑周围。农学家刚刚使用一架混合式无人机飞越田地，该无人机通过螺旋桨起降，但利用固定翼保持距离和速度以扫描广阔的公顷土地。

paragraphs.text: The UAV is fitted with a four spectral band precision sensor that conducts onboard processing immediately after the flight, allowing farmers and field staff to address, almost immediately, any crop abnormalities that the sensor may have recorded, making the data collection truly real-time.
paragraphs.translation: 该无人机配备了一个四光谱波段精密传感器，可在飞行后立即进行机载处理，使农民和现场工作人员能够几乎立即处理传感器可能记录到的任何作物异常，使数据收集真正实时。

paragraphs.text: In this instance, the farmers and agronomists are looking for specialized software to give them an accurate plant population count. It's been 10 days since the corn emerged and the farmer wants to determine if there are any parts of the field that require replanting due to a lack of emergence or wind damage, which can be severe in the early stages of the summer rainy season.
paragraphs.translation: 在这种情况下，农民和农学家正在寻找专门的软件来提供准确的植物种群计数。玉米出苗已有10天，农民想要确定田地是否有任何部分因出苗不足或风害需要补种，风害在夏季雨季初期可能很严重。

paragraphs.text: At this growth stage of the plant's development, the farmer has another 10 days to conduct any replanting before the majority of his fertilizer and chemical applications need to occur. Once these have been applied, it becomes economically unviable to take corrective action, making any further collected data historical and useful only to inform future practices for the season to come.
paragraphs.translation: 在植物生长的这一阶段，农民还有10天时间进行任何补种，然后大部分肥料和化学药剂需要施用。一旦施用后，采取纠正措施在经济上变得不可行，使得任何进一步收集的数据成为历史数据，仅可用于指导未来的季节实践。

paragraphs.text: The software completes its processing in under 15 minutes producing a plant population count map. It's difficult to grasp just how impressive this is, without understanding that just over a year ago it would have taken three to five days to process the exact same data set, illustrating the advancements that have been achieved in precision agriculture and remote sensing in recent years. With the software having been developed in the United States on the same variety of crops in seemingly similar conditions, the agronomist feels confident that the software will produce a near accurate result.
paragraphs.translation: 该软件在不到15分钟内完成处理，生成植物种群计数地图。如果不了解仅仅一年多前处理完全相同的数据集需要三到五天，就很难理解这有多令人印象深刻，这说明了近年来在精准农业和遥感方面取得的进步。由于该软件是在美国针对类似条件下相同作物品种开发的，农学家相信软件会产生接近准确的结果。

paragraphs.text: As the map appears on the screen, the agronomist's face begins to drop. Having walked through the planted rows before the flight to gain a physical understanding of the situation on the ground, he knows the instant he sees the data on his screen that the plant count is not correct, and so do the farmers, even with their limited understanding of how to read remote sensing maps.
paragraphs.translation: 当地图出现在屏幕上时，农学家的脸色开始沉下来。在飞行前，他已经走过种植行，以实地了解情况，因此他一看到屏幕上的数据就知道植物计数不正确，农民们也是如此，尽管他们对如何解读遥感地图的了解有限。

paragraphs.text: Hypothetically, it is possible for machines to learn to solve any problem on earth relating to the physical interaction of all things within a defined or contained environment by using artificial intelligence and machine learning.
paragraphs.translation: 假设上，通过使用人工智能和机器学习，机器有可能学习解决地球上任何与在界定或封闭环境中所有事物物理交互相关的问题。

paragraphs.text: Remote sensors enable algorithms (算法) to interpret a field's environment as statistical data that can be understood and useful to farmers for decision-making. Algorithms process the data, adapting and learning based on the data received. The more inputs and statistical information collected, the better the algorithm will be at predicting a range of outcomes. And the aim is that farmers can use this artificial intelligence to achieve their goal of a better harvest through making better decisions in the field.
paragraphs.translation: 远程传感器使算法能够将田地环境解读为统计数据，这些数据对农民来说是可理解且有助于决策的。算法处理数据，根据接收到的数据进行适应和学习。收集的输入和统计信息越多，算法预测一系列结果的能力就越强。目标是农民可以利用这种人工智能通过更好地在田间决策来实现更好的收成。

paragraphs.text: In 2011, IBM, through its R&D Headquarters in Haifa, Israel, launched an agricultural cloud computing project. The project, in collaboration with a number of specialized IT and agricultural partners, had one goal in mind—to take a variety of academic and physical data sources from an agricultural environment and turn these into automatic predictive solutions for farmers that would assist them in making real-time decisions in the field.
paragraphs.translation: 2011年，IBM通过其位于以色列海法的研发总部启动了一个农业云计算项目。该项目与多个专业IT和农业合作伙伴合作，有一个目标：从农业环境中获取各种学术和物理数据源，并将这些转化为自动预测解决方案，帮助农民在田间进行实时决策。

paragraphs.text: Interviews with some of the IBM project team members at the time revealed that the team believed it was entirely possible to "algorithm" agriculture, meaning that algorithms could solve any problem in the world. Earlier that year, IBM's cognitive learning system, Watson, competed in the game Jeopardy against former winners Brad Rutter and Ken Jennings with astonishing results. Several years later, Watson went on to produce ground-breaking achievements in the field of medicine.
paragraphs.translation: 当时对一些IBM项目团队成员的采访显示，团队相信完全有可能“算法化”农业，意思是算法可以解决世界上的任何问题。同年早些时候，IBM的认知学习系统Watson与前任冠军Brad Rutter和Ken Jennings在游戏《危险边缘》中竞争，取得了惊人成果。几年后，Watson在医学领域取得了突破性成就。

paragraphs.text: So why did the project have such success in medicine but not agriculture? Because it is one of the most difficult fields to contain for the purpose of statistical quantification. Even within a single field, conditions are always changing from one section to the next. There's unpredictable weather, changes in soil quality, and the ever-present possibility that pests and diseases may pay a visit. Growers may feel their prospects are good for an upcoming harvest, but until that day arrives, the outcome will always be uncertain.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，为什么该项目在医学上如此成功，但在农业上却没有呢？因为农业是最难为统计量化目的而控制的领域之一。即使在一个田地内，条件也总是从一个部分到另一个部分不断变化。有不可预测的天气、土壤质量的变化，以及病虫害随时可能发生的可能性。种植者可能觉得即将到来的收成前景良好，但在那天到来之前，结果总是不确定的。

paragraphs.text: By comparison, our bodies are a contained environment. Agriculture takes place in nature, among ecosystems of interacting organisms and activity, and crop production takes place within that ecosystem environment. But these ecosystems are not contained. They are subject to climatic occurrences such as weather systems, which impact upon hemispheres as a whole, and from continent to continent. Therefore, understanding how to manage an agricultural environment means taking literally many hundreds if not thousands of factors into account.
paragraphs.translation: 相比之下，我们的身体是一个封闭环境。农业发生在自然界中，在相互作用的生物体和活动的生态系统中，作物生产发生在这种生态系统环境中。但这些生态系统不是封闭的。它们受到气候事件的影响，如天气系统，这些系统影响整个半球，甚至跨越大陆。因此，理解如何管理农业环境意味着要考虑到数百甚至数千个因素。

paragraphs.text: What may occur with the same seed and fertilizer program in the United States' Midwest region is almost certainly unrelated to what may occur with the same seed and fertilizer program in Australia or South Africa. A few factors that could impact on variation would typically include the measurement of rain per unit of a crop planted, soil type, patterns of soil degradation, daylight hours, temperature and so forth.
paragraphs.translation: 在美国中西部地区使用相同种子和肥料计划可能发生的情况，几乎肯定与在澳大利亚或南非使用相同种子和肥料计划可能发生的情况无关。一些可能影响变化的因素通常包括每单位种植作物的降雨量测量、土壤类型、土壤退化模式、日照时间、温度等。

paragraphs.text: So the problem with deploying machine learning and artificial intelligence in agriculture is not that scientists lack the capacity to develop programs and protocols to begin to address the biggest of growers' concerns; the problem is that in most cases, no two environments will be exactly alike, which makes the testing, validation and successful rollout of such technologies much more laborious than in most other industries.
paragraphs.translation: 因此，在农业中部署机器学习和人工智能的问题不在于科学家缺乏开发程序和协议以开始解决种植者最大关切的能力；问题在于，在大多数情况下，没有两个环境是完全相同的，这使得这些技术的测试、验证和成功推广比大多数其他行业更加费力。

paragraphs.text: Practically, to say that Al and Machine Learning can be developed to solve all problems related to our physical environment is to basically say that we have a complete understanding of all aspects of the interaction of physical or material activity on the planet. After all, it is only through our understanding of 'the nature of things' that protocols and processes are designed for the rational capabilities of cognitive systems to take place. And, although Al and Machine Learning are teaching us many things about how to understand our environment, we are still far from being able to predict critical outcomes in fields like agriculture purely through the cognitive ability of machines.
paragraphs.translation: 实际上，说人工智能和机器学习可以被开发来解决与我们物理环境相关的所有问题，基本上是在说我们对地球上物理或物质活动交互的所有方面有完全的理解。毕竟，只有通过我们对‘事物本质’的理解，才能设计协议和流程，让认知系统的合理能力得以发挥。而且，尽管人工智能和机器学习正在教我们许多关于如何理解环境的知识，但我们仍然远不能纯粹通过机器的认知能力来预测像农业这样的领域的关键结果。

paragraphs.text: Backed by the venture capital community, which is now investing billions of dollars in the sector, most agricultural technology startups today are pushed to complete development as quickly as possible and then encouraged to flood the market as quickly as possible with their products.
paragraphs.translation: 在风险投资界的支持下，目前该行业投资数十亿美元，今天大多数农业科技初创公司被推动尽快完成开发，然后鼓励尽快将产品推向市场。

paragraphs.text: This usually results in a failure of a product, which leads to skepticism from the market and delivers a blow to the integrity of Machine Learning technology. In most cases, the problem is not that the technology does not work, the problem is that industry has not taken the time to respect that agriculture is one of the most uncontained environments to manage. For technology to truly make an impact on agriculture, more effort, skills, and funding is needed to test these technologies in farmers' fields.
paragraphs.translation: 这通常导致产品失败，引起市场的怀疑，并打击了机器学习技术的完整性。在大多数情况下，问题不在于技术不起作用，而在于行业没有花时间尊重农业是最不受控制的环境之一。要让技术真正对农业产生影响，需要更多的努力、技能和资金在农民的田间测试这些技术。

paragraphs.text: There is huge potential for artificial intelligence and machine learning to revolutionize agriculture by integrating these technologies into critical markets on a global scale. Only then can it make a difference to the grower, where it really counts.
paragraphs.translation: 通过将人工智能和机器学习整合到全球关键市场中，这些技术有巨大潜力彻底改变农业。只有这样，才能对种植者产生影响，在真正重要的地方。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: What is the place of art in a culture of inattention? Recent visitors to the Louvre report that tourists can now spend only a minute in front of the Mona Lisa before being asked to move on. Much of that time, for some of them, is spent taking photographs not even of the painting but of themselves with the painting in the background.
paragraphs.translation: 在注意力分散的文化中，艺术的地位是什么？最近参观卢浮宫的游客报告说，游客现在在《蒙娜丽莎》前只能停留一分钟，然后就被要求离开。对于其中一些人来说，大部分时间都花在拍照上，甚至不是拍画作，而是以画作为背景自拍。

paragraphs.text: One view is that we have democratised tourism and gallery-going so much that we have made it effectively impossible to appreciate what we've travelled to see. In this oversubscribed society, experience becomes a commodity like any other. There are queues to climb Mt. Jolmo Lungma as well as to see famous paintings. Leisure, thus conceived, is hard labour, and returning to work becomes a well-earned break from the ordeal.
paragraphs.translation: 一种观点认为，我们已经将旅游和参观画廊民主化到如此程度，以至于实际上无法欣赏我们专程去看的东西。在这个过度拥挤的社会中，经验变成了一种像其他商品一样的商品。攀登珠穆朗玛峰和观看名画都需要排队。如此概念化的休闲是艰苦劳动，而返回工作则成了从这种磨难中挣来的休息。

paragraphs.text: What gets lost in this industrialised haste is the quality of looking. Consider an extreme example, the late philosopher Richard Wollheim. When he visited the Louvre he could spend as much as four hours sitting before a painting. The first hour, he claimed, was necessary for misperceptions to be eliminated. It was only then that the picture would begin to disclose itself. This seems unthinkable today, but it is still possible to organise. Even in the busiest museums there are many rooms and many pictures worth hours of contemplation which the crowds largely ignore. Sometimes the largest crowds are partly the products of bad management; the Mona Lisa is such a hurried experience today partly because the museum is being reorganised. The Uffizi in Florence, another site of cultural pilgrimage, has cut its entry queues down to seven minutes by clever management. And there are some forms of art, those designed to be spectacles as well as objects of contemplation, which can work perfectly well in the face of huge crowds.
paragraphs.translation: 在这种工业化的匆忙中失去的是观看的质量。考虑一个极端例子，已故哲学家理查德·沃尔海姆。当他参观卢浮宫时，他能在一幅画前坐上四个小时。他声称，第一个小时是消除误解所必需的。只有到那时，画面才开始展现自身。这在今天似乎难以想象，但仍然是可以组织的。即使在最繁忙的博物馆，也有许多房间和许多画作值得花上几小时沉思，而人群大多忽略。有时，最大的人群部分是由于管理不善造成的；《蒙娜丽莎》今天如此匆忙的体验，部分原因是博物馆正在重组。佛罗伦萨的乌菲兹美术馆，另一个文化朝圣地，通过聪明的管理将入口排队时间缩短到七分钟。还有一些艺术形式，那些设计为奇观和沉思对象的，可以在面对巨大人群时完美运作。

paragraphs.text: Olafur Eliasson's current Tate Modern show, for instance, might seem nothing more than an entertainment, overrun as it is with kids romping (喧闹地玩耍) in fog rooms and spray mist installations. But it's more than that: where Eliasson is at his most entertaining, he is at his most serious too, and his disorienting installations bring home the reality of the destructive effects we are having on the planet—not least what we are doing to the glaciers of Eliasson's beloved Iceland.
paragraphs.translation: 例如，奥拉维尔·埃利亚松当前在泰特现代美术馆的展览，可能看起来只是一种娱乐，因为孩子们在雾室和喷雾装置中嬉闹（喧闹地玩耍）。但它不止于此：在埃利亚松最娱乐的地方，他也最严肃，他那令人迷失方向的装置让我们直面我们对地球的破坏性影响的现实——尤其是我们对埃利亚松钟爱的冰岛冰川所做的事情。

paragraphs.text: Marcel Proust, another lover of the Louvre, wrote- "It is only through art that we can escape from ourselves and know how another person sees the universe, whose landscapes would otherwise have remained as unknown as any on the moon." If any art remains worth seeing, it must lead us to such escapes. But a minute in front of a painting in a hurried crowd won't do that.
paragraphs.translation: 马塞尔·普鲁斯特，另一位卢浮宫的爱好者，写道：“只有通过艺术，我们才能逃离自我，并了解另一个人如何看待宇宙，否则其景观将如同月球上的任何地方一样未知。”如果还有艺术值得观看，它必须引领我们进行这样的逃离。但在匆忙人群中，在一幅画前停留一分钟是做不到的。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Every five years, the government tries to tell Americans what to put in their bellies. Eat more vegetables. Dial back the fats. It's all based on the best available science for leading a healthy life. But the best available science also has a lot to say about what those food choices do to the environment, and some researchers are annoyed that new dietary recommendations of the USDA (United States Department of Agriculture) released yesterday seem to utterly ignore that fact.
paragraphs.translation: 每五年，政府都会试图告诉美国人该吃什么。多吃蔬菜。减少脂肪摄入。这一切都基于引领健康生活的最佳可用科学。但最佳可用科学也对这些食物选择对环境的影响有很多说法，一些研究人员对昨天发布的美国农业部（USDA）的新饮食建议似乎完全忽略这一事实感到恼火。

paragraphs.text: Broadly, the 2016-2020 dietary recommendations aim for balance: more vegetables, leaner meats and far less sugar.
paragraphs.translation: 总体而言，2016-2020年的饮食建议旨在实现平衡：更多的蔬菜、更瘦的肉类和少得多的糖。

paragraphs.text: But Americans consume more calories per capita than almost any other country in the world. So the things Americans eat have a huge impact on climate change. Soil tilling releases carbon dioxide, and delivery vehicles emit exhaust. The government's dietary guidelines could have done a lot to lower that climate cost. Not just because of their position of authority: The guidelines drive billions of dollars of food production through federal programs like school lunches and nutrition assistance for the needy.
paragraphs.translation: 但美国人均卡路里消耗量高于世界上几乎任何其他国家。因此，美国人吃的东西对气候变化有很大影响。土壤耕作释放二氧化碳，运输车辆排放废气。政府的饮食指南本可以大大降低这种气候成本。这不仅是因为它们的权威地位：这些指南通过学校午餐和对贫困人群的营养援助等联邦项目推动数十亿美元的食品生产。

paragraphs.text: On its own, plant and animal agriculture contributes 9 percent of all the country's greenhouse gas emissions. That's not counting the fuel burned in transportation, processing, refrigeration, and other waypoints between farm and belly. Red meats are among the biggest and most notorious emitters, but trucking a salad from California to Minnesota in January also carries a significant burden. And greenhouse gas emissions aren't the whole story. Food production is the largest user of fresh water, largest contributor to the loss of biodiversity, and a major contributor to using up natural resources.
paragraphs.translation: 仅植物和动物农业就贡献了全国温室气体排放的9%。这还不包括在运输、加工、冷藏以及从农场到餐桌之间的其他环节中燃烧的燃料。红肉是最大和最臭名昭著的排放者之一，但在一月份用卡车将沙拉从加利福尼亚州运到明尼苏达州也带来显著负担。温室气体排放还不是全部。食品生产是淡水的最大用户，是生物多样性丧失的最大贡献者，也是耗尽自然资源的主要贡献者。

paragraphs.text: All of these points and more showed up in the Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee's scientific report, released last February. Miriam Nelson chaired the subcommittee in charge of sustainability for the report, and is disappointed that eating less meat and buying local food aren't in the final product. "Especially, if you consider that eating less meat, especially red and processed, has health benefits," she says.
paragraphs.translation: 所有这些观点以及更多内容都出现在去年二月发布的《饮食指南咨询委员会》的科学报告中。米里亚姆·尼尔森主持了该报告中负责可持续性的小组委员会，并对最终产品中没有包括少吃肉类和购买本地食品感到失望。“尤其是，如果你考虑到少吃肉类，特别是红肉和加工肉类，对健康有益，”她说。

paragraphs.text: So what happened? The official response is that sustainability falls too far outside the guidelines' official scope, which is to provide "nutritional and dietary information."
paragraphs.translation: 那么发生了什么？官方回应是，可持续性过于偏离指南的官方范围，即提供“营养和饮食信息”。

paragraphs.text: Possibly the agencies in charge of drafting the decisions are too close to the industries they are supposed to regulate. On one hand, the USDA is compiling dietary advice. On the other, their clients are US agriculture companies.
paragraphs.translation: 可能负责起草决策的机构过于接近它们本应监管的行业。一方面，美国农业部在编写饮食建议；另一方面，它们的客户是美国农业公司。

paragraphs.text: The line about keeping the guidelines' scope to nutrition and diet doesn't ring quite right with researchers. David Wallinga, for example, says, "In previous guidelines, they've always been concerned with things like food security—which is presumably the mission of the USDA. You absolutely need to be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability if you want secure food in the future."
paragraphs.translation: 关于将指南范围限制在营养和饮食上的说法，研究人员并不完全认同。例如，大卫·瓦林加说：“在之前的指南中，他们一直关注诸如粮食安全等问题——这大概是美国农业部的使命。如果你想要未来的粮食安全，你绝对需要担心气候影响和未来的可持续性。”
